_about: Every decision rule Walo uses, with its source. Crop-specific values live in data/crops.json (eco = FAO EcoCrop, fao56 = FAO-56 Tables 11/12, heat/gdd below). Values marked default:true have no single standard; they are Walo's labelled choice and can be changed here without touching the code.

FAO56.title: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. FAO, Rome. Eq. 6 (Penman-Monteith ET0), Eq. 7-13, 21-39; Tables 11 and 12.

USDA_SCS.title: USDA Soil Conservation Service effective rainfall method as implemented in FAO CROPWAT (Smith 1992, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 46): Peff = P(125 - 0.2P)/125 for P <= 250 mm/month, else 125 + 0.1P.

FREREPOPOV.title: Frère, M. & Popov, G.F. (1979). Agrometeorological crop monitoring and forecasting. FAO Plant Production and Protection Paper 17. FAO, Rome (Water Requirement Satisfaction Index, WRSI).

FAO_AEZ.title: FAO (1978). Report on the Agro-ecological Zones Project, Vol. 1: Methodology and results for Africa. World Soil Resources Report 48 (growing period: months with rain >= 0.5 x potential evapotranspiration).

SIVAKUMAR88.title: Sivakumar, M.V.K. (1988). Predicting rainy season potential from the onset of rains in Southern Sahelian and Sudanian climatic zones of West Africa. Agricultural and Forest Meteorology 42: 295-305 (onset: >= 20 mm in 3 days, no dry spell > 7 days in the next 30 days).

STERN82.title: Stern, R.D., Dennett, M.D. & Dale, I.C. (1982). Analysing daily rainfall measurements to give agronomically useful results. I. Direct methods. Experimental Agriculture 18: 223-236 (onset = first date after a fixed start date meeting a rain and dry-spell rule; percentiles across years).

ECOCROP.title: FAO EcoCrop database; suitability method of Hijmans et al. (2001) DIVA-GIS and Ramirez-Villegas, Jarvis & Läderach (2013) Agricultural and Forest Meteorology 170: 67-78 (suitability 1 inside the optimum range, falling linearly to 0 at the absolute limits; overall = minimum of temperature and rain suitability).

FAO76.title: FAO (1976). A framework for land evaluation. FAO Soils Bulletin 32 (suitability classes S1 highly, S2 moderately, S3 marginally suitable, N not suitable).

SANCHEZ14.title: Sánchez, B., Rasmussen, A. & Porter, J.R. (2014). Temperatures and the growth and development of maize and rice: a review. Global Change Biology 20: 408-417 (maize and rice: reproductive damage above about 35 °C).

MCMASTER97.title: McMaster, G.S. & Wilhelm, W.W. (1997). Growing degree-days: one equation, two interpretations. Agricultural and Forest Meteorology 87: 291-300 (GDD = max(0, (Tmax + Tmin)/2 - Tbase); maize Tbase 10 °C with 30 °C upper cut-off).

POWER.title: NASA POWER daily API, AG community: PRECTOTCORR, T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, WS2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, 1991-2025.

MODIS.title: Didan, K. (2021). MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061 (MOD13Q1). NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC. doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061. Accessed via Microsoft Planetary Computer.

METEOMATICS.title: Meteomatics Weather API, daily precip_24h and t_max_2m_24h, model mix (forecast only; NASA POWER remains the climatology and history).

et0.method: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith, daily, from NASA POWER Tmax, Tmin, RH2M, WS2M (2 m), ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN; site elevation from POWER

growing_period.humid_note: Humid period: months where rain exceeds ET0 (FAO AEZ). Used for 'harvest month is usually wet' (drying risk).

major_search.note: No single standard start date for Ghana; Sivakumar (1988) searched from 1 May in the Sahel. Walo starts at 1 March so the forest and transition zones are not missed.

minor_search.note: Second (minor) season searched only in the bimodal zones (FAO zone text: forest, transition, coastal savanna).

water.store_note: Plant-available water in the root zone at sowing is unknown; Walo assumes a 100 mm bucket that starts empty and fills with effective rain (FAO WRSI practice uses soil water-holding capacity; no farm soil test).

wrsi_classes.label: Crop likely to fail without water

water.wrsi_note: WRSI = 100 x actual / required crop water use over the season. Below 50 is associated with crop failure (Frère & Popov 1979).
water.wrsi_dots_note: WRSI mapped to the same dots: >=80 -> 5 (S1), 60-80 -> 4 (S2), 50-60 -> 3 (S3), <50 -> 1 (N). Walo mapping (labelled default).
water.wrsi_max_note: WRSI was built for rain-fed seasonal crops (cereals, legumes). For longer crops (cassava, plantain) Walo shows the water numbers but does not use them for the class. Labelled default.
water._wrsi_dots_note: Dots follow the water classes above: enough rain = 5, any water stress = 3 ("can grow", not "grows well"), likely to fail without water = 1. A season with 60-79% of its water need is a stressed crop, so it must not read as "grows well".

suitability.classes_note: FAO (1976) defines the classes but not numeric cut-offs; Walo splits the 0-1 EcoCrop index at 0.8 / 0.6 / 0.4 / 0.2.
suitability.combine: Shown class = the lower of the EcoCrop class and the FAO-56 water class (WRSI at the usual onset) for seasonal crops with FAO-56 values.
suitability.method: EcoCrop (Ramirez-Villegas et al. 2013): for each of the 12 possible start months, growing season = round(mean(cycle_days.min, cycle_days.max) / 30) months (max 12). Temperature suitability = lowest monthly value in the season (mean temperature against abs_min, opt_min, opt_max, abs_max, linear in between); the best start month is kept. Rain suitability = the place's annual rain against the EcoCrop rain limits, because the FAO EcoCrop database gives those limits as annual rainfall (deviation from the season-total form; see DESIGN.md Methods). Suitability = temperature x rain.

heat.default_note: Where no crop-specific critical temperature is cited, Walo uses the top of the crop's EcoCrop optimum temperature range.
heat.hot_day_note: Days above 35 °C shown in 'then vs now' and month cards (the maize and rice critical temperature, Sánchez et al. 2014).
heat.count_note: Hot-day counts (days with Tmax above each whole degree) are stored per month so any crop's threshold can be looked up.

gdd.default_note: Other crops: the EcoCrop absolute minimum temperature is used as base temperature (no upper cut-off).
gdd.use: Farm stage = heat units since sowing (NASA POWER daily when available) / heat units the FAO-56 stage lengths need at that place in a normal year.

sell.rule: Show 'Harvest & sell' from the start of the FAO-56 late-season stage (heat units). Crops without FAO-56 stages use stages_default.

store_window_months.note: How far after harvest Walo looks for the usual price peak when it says 'store if you can'. Walo default (grain and dried crops keep about this long in a good store).

store_gain_min.note: Walo says 'store if you can' only when the usual price in the best month is at least 10% above the harvest month (WFP seasonal index). Walo default.

best_guess_months_after_harvest.note: Crops with no price series: sell about 3 months after harvest, when stores run low. Walo default, from the usual pattern of crops that do have price data.

compare_max_km.note: Other markets compared with the nearest one only within this straight-line distance. Walo default.

compare_gain_min.note: A market is named as 'usually pays more' only if its last-12-months average is at least 15% above the nearest market, same crop and unit. Walo default.

season_days_default.note: Only for crops with neither a local season length nor an EcoCrop cycle (none at present).

stages_default.note: Stage starts (share of the season) for crops without FAO-56 stage lengths (yam, cocoyam, okra, cashew): the mean split of the FAO-56 Table 11 rows Walo uses (initial 18%, development 25%, mid 37%, late 21%).

ndvi.note: NDVI within ±0.05 of the 2016–2025 mean for that month is shown as 'about usual'. Walo default (MODIS NDVI noise is a few hundredths).

field_risk._about: Weather-driven pest and disease pressure at one field, used by the tips on the field screen. These are extension rules of thumb applied to the field, not a model of a named disease and not crop-specific.

rh_wet.note: Air this humid keeps leaves wet for hours, which is the condition leaf and pod fungi need in order to spread.

rh_dry.note: Air this dry, in a week with little rain, is when thrips and mites build up.

dry7_mm.note: Rain below this over seven days counts as a dry week.
